item.title: Wrongful Death Settlement: Brown family secures $5 million; claims against Walgreens remain pending
item.description: The family of Banko Brown, a Black transgender man fatally shot by a security guard, has secured a $5 million settlement related to claims against the guard and his employer. However, the legal battle continues, as the family's lawsuit against Walgreens and Allied Universal Security Services remains unresolved in court.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr back new Beatles attraction in Liverpool; will support young local artists
item.description: Liverpool is set to unveil a major Beatles attraction by 2028, championed by Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr. This expansive 100,000-square-foot venue will replace the Beatles Story at Albert Dock, featuring immersive exhibits designed to boost tourism. A portion of ticket sales will support local artists via the Apple Corps Liverpool Trust, aiming to celebrate young talent and align with the premiere of four Beatles films in April 2028.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Michigan woman wins $1 million Powerball prize, plans to pay off her mortgage
item.description: Alisa Moore, hailing from Hazel Park, Michigan, recently struck gold by winning a staggering $1 million in the Powerball lottery. She bought her lucky ticket while exiting a Kroger store on October 19. The next day, after thoroughly checking her ticket, she confirmed her fortune. Instead of indulging in luxury, Moore aims to settle her mortgage and wisely invest the leftover amount, showcasing her savvy handling of unexpected wealth.

item.title: Guinness Verification Pending: Warren Crawford bowls 243 strikes; fundraiser raises $20,000
item.description: Warren Crawford stunned everyone with his astounding bowling prowess, clocking in 243 strikes within a single hour at a charity event that benefitted veterans and first responders. The endeavor successfully garnered around $20,000 in donations. Utilizing a unique two-handed bowling style he honed since childhood, Crawford's incredible achievement now awaits verification from Guinness World Records, all amidst the electrifying support of the audience.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Roger Daltrey's cancer charity concerts reach 150 shows, raising over £36 million since 2000
item.description: The Teenage Cancer Trust celebrated its 150th concert at London's Royal Albert Hall, raising over £36 million. Founded by Roger Daltrey in 2000, the series features numerous well-known musicians supporting young people with cancer. Performers such as Manic Street Preachers and Elbow participated in the recent program curated by Robert Smith. The charity emphasizes the importance of specialized care for patients aged 13 to 24 during treatment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Teens who met on holiday in 1994 reunite 20 years later and marry
item.description: It was in the sun-soaked summer of 1994 when David McArdle encountered Jodie while vacationing in Kos, Greece. Their brief encounter ignited a beautiful friendship carried through pen letters for three years. Life scattered them, but fate intervened after twenty years when Jodie reached out to David's mother. Their profound reconnection blossomed into love, culminating in a proposal atop the London Eye.

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries faces first test in bid to become first Black US House speaker
item.description: As Hakeem Jeffries gears up for a historic election, he prepares to potentially become the first black Speaker of the House, vying for the nomination from House Democrats. Acknowledging calls for change in leadership, Jeffries is proactively connecting with diverse caucuses to build support. His potential victory aligns with other momentous leadership changes, reflecting the priorities of newly elected lawmakers eager to push legislative agendas before their official induction.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Island Nations Seek Climate Funding: States press for emissions cuts; seek $700 million for resilience
item.description: Small island nations are urgently calling for action at climate negotiations due to the exacerbating threats of global warming. Their leaders stress the essential need for financial aid from wealthier nations, which contribute most to pollution. This call for unity among these nations is becoming increasingly crucial. Young representatives advocate for climate justice and demand accountability from world leaders, as COP31 seeks to reinforce commitments to effectively tackle climate change.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Tennessee studio estate where Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton recorded lists for $19.5 million
item.description: Dark Horse Estate in Franklin, Tennessee is now on the market for $19.5 million. This unique property features recording facilities and accommodations for artists and guests alike. It has a rich history with over 65 gold and platinum albums recorded by various notable musicians. The estate spans over 10 acres, providing privacy and ample outdoor space for inspiration and relaxation.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Rare dinosaur discovery: Palaeontologists may uncover new dinosaur species; fossil from Utah to be studied in Raleigh's Dino Lab
item.description: The North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences in Raleigh is buzzing with excitement over a rare dinosaur skeleton recently acquired. Dating back 75 million years, and reminiscent of a large ostrich, this find from Utah could represent a new species, subject to further investigation. Visitors have the unique opportunity to view live research in the Dino Lab, offering insights into the diversity of dinosaurs from this area.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Caltech robot revolutionizes space: Caltech robot builds structure in space; Space assembly showcases future construction possibilities
item.description: A robot developed by researchers at California Institute of Technology constructed a segment of a space structure autonomously. The assembly occurred as part of DARPA's NOM4D programme, testing innovative techniques for space construction. The Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly robot utilized individual components to build an experimental antenna. Following the launch, the robot successfully coordinated with Earth-based commands to assemble its structure in orbit.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: 'Responsibility to banish hatred': Mamdani condemns anti-Indian racism at Diwali event
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani addressed rising incidents of racism targeting the Indian-American community during a Diwali celebration. He emphasized the need for collective responsibility in combating hate and ensuring safety for Hindus and Sikhs. Thirteen US lawmakers have requested a federal investigation into a disruption of a Diwali event in Seattle. They referred to troubling patterns of anti-South Asian hate across the country.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: 'Big potential benefit': Putin backs trilateral talks with Trump, Xi on APEC sidelines
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin expects substantial benefits from the upcoming trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The discussions are set to occur during the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China. Putin aims to strengthen Russia's diplomatic position while addressing the war in Ukraine. However, there are differing agendas that could complicate the talks, particularly regarding nuclear disarmament.

item.title: 'Human': Cambridge’s 'word of the year' is a counterbalance to AI
item.description: Cambridge Dictionary selected 'human' as its Word of the Year for 2026 based on significant trends. This reflects a growing recognition of human creativity, emotion, and connection amidst pervasive artificial intelligence. The increased use of terms like 'human-written' indicates a shift in how people value content. There is evidence that consumers are drawn to products with human involvement and craftsmanship.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Dua Lipa’s £6.75m London home still under renovation, with 2027 finish date
item.description: Dua Lipa has been deeply involved in the extensive renovation of her north London Victorian home, which she bought back in 2020. The project has hit snags due to planning disputes and environmental issues tied to the conservation area. Currently, intensive excavation is underway with hopes for several leisure and artistic areas. Unfortunately, the anticipated completion has now been delayed until July 2027, leaving the site buzzing with construction activity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Michigan woman loses appeal for larger share of marital wealth after 2018 $705,000 deal
item.description: In a recent court case, Cassandra Fameux from Michigan aimed to obtain a greater portion of her divorce settlement. She argued that a property agreement worth $705,000, signed during her guardianship, was unjust. However, the appeals court affirmed the earlier ruling, confirming the agreement's binding nature. The court dismissed her claims of undue pressure, leaving her with far less than the nearly $1 million she anticipated.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
